back: Reduced Instruction Set Computer: few simple, fixed-length instructions, mostly one cycle each, many registers, load-store.
Complex Instruction Set Computer: many powerful, variable-length instructions taking several cycles, fewer registers.
Overlapping the stages of different instructions so that more instructions are completed per second.
n instructions on k stages take n + k − 1 cycles; without a pipeline n × k.
Pipelining raises throughput; the time for one instruction does not fall.
After a jump, the instructions already fetched may be wrong and are discarded, wasting cycles.
Many registers keep data inside the processor, avoiding slow memory accesses.
Instructions in the pipeline must be completed or discarded and the resume address recorded.
